title: 5 agents
blurb: A lead and five subagents on two Branches at once: each mounts its own Workspace, stale Workspaces merge on commit, .lww makes build output last-writer-wins, and two agents change the same line. The lead merges and publishes.

root.say: Two feature Branches, checkout and search, each with .lww so dependencies and build output never conflict.
root.note: A fork is metadata only. .lww includes .gitignore: node_modules and .next become last-writer-wins.

subagent.prompt: On the checkout Branch: install the dependencies and build in a Workspace of your own, commit, and report.
On the checkout Branch: add the cart page (app/cart/page.tsx) and add --lint to the build script, commit, and report.
On the checkout Branch: add the API route (app/api/route.ts), add --profile to the build script, build, commit, and report.

root.note: ben and cy change the same line of package.json: whoever commits second gets a Conflict in its Workspace.

subagent.prompt: On the search Branch: add the search page (app/search/page.tsx), install, build and test, commit, and report.
On the search Branch: add the tokenizer (lib/tokenize.ts), test the Branch, and report.

root.reply: Five agents are working: ava, ben and cy on checkout; dee and eli on search.

root.say: All five reported. A last look at who is where.
Merging checkout and search into release and publishing it.
root.note: Both Branches installed and built: .lww takes the newer build output instead of a conflict.

root.reply: release is on main: the cart, the API route, search and the tokenizer, with both build flags. Five agents, two Branches, one Store.

ava.say: Mounting checkout to install and build.

ava.reply: checkout has the dependencies and a build, committed.

ben.say: Mounting checkout for the cart page and the lint flag.

ben.reply: checkout has the cart page and --lint in the build script.

cy.say: Mounting checkout for the API route and the profile flag.

cy.reply: checkout has the API route and --profile in the build script.

dee.say: Mounting search for the search page; then install, build and test.

bash.description: Search page; build and test on search

dee.reply: search has the search page, built and tested.

eli.say: Writing the tokenizer with fs, then testing search in a Sandbox.

eli.reply: search has the tokenizer, and the tests pass.
